newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Arrests over Budapest bombs, mayor says city tense.
newsitem.headline: Arrests over Budapest bombs, mayor says city tense.

text.p: Hungarian police said on Friday they had arrested two suspects in a wave of bombings and shootings that Budapest's mayor attributes to gang warfare.
"This is a war, this is definitely a gang war," Mayor Gabor Demszky told Reuters shortly before police announced the arrests of two men identified only as Peter S. and Laszlo R.

Police said that after arresting the two men on November 5, they confiscated handguns, silencers, 1,000 rounds of ammunition, seven hand grenades, 2.5 kg (5.5 lb) of plastic explosive and a timing device during a search of a house used by Peter S.

"One of the hand grenades was of the same type as the one used in the bombing of the Leroy Country Pub on Wednesday," police Colonel Janos Lazar of the Hungarian National Police told a news conference.

Since the summer, a series of grenade blasts has caused minor damage outside more than a dozen pubs, nightclubs and restaurants. The grenades were set off late at night, when few patrons were around, and no one was injured.
But Demszky said: "There is a tension in the city because of this and everybody is waiting and demanding safety measures."
Earlier this month underworld boss Jozsef Prisztas was shot dead with a pistol at point-blank range as he sat in his jeep.
Police also are investigating the shooting and wounding at Budapest's race track on Wednesday of one of the city's major racehorse owners.
Csaba Lakatos was shot three times with a rifle while he was walking in the stable area between races. "We are presently questioning Lakatos in hospital," Lazar said.

Demszky said the violence could be linked to mob figures from countries such as Ukraine and Russia. Police also have theorised that the underworld is in upheaval over the disappearance of a gangland "investment banker" who absconded with three billion forints ($200 million).
